page: Amazon Web Services m5.large is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. It operates on an x86_64 architecture featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8175M processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped across 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads via hyperthreading. Memory is allocated at 8.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached block storage, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without dedicated complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the entry-level 2-vCPU resource envelope, showing lower-tier compute and memory throughput compared to larger or modern instances. In compute workloads, the instance achieved a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 1023.0 and a multi-core score of 1212.0, along with a PassMark CPU score of 1995.98. Single-threaded tasks benefit from instruction support such as AVX-512F and AES-NI, logging 21.26 GB/sec in gzip compression. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers 13.29 GB/sec for reads and 11.49 GB/sec for writes. Application tests record Redis throughput of 1.65 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.94 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the m5.large configuration lies in its reliance on external storage and its single physical core constraint, which caps parallel processing capabilities under sustained load. However, the 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides predictable, stable memory per thread for moderate workloads without paying for larger multi-core instances. This profile is best suited for small web services, microservices, light background workers, development environments, and low-traffic application servers requiring dedicated hypervisor scheduling rather than burstable CPU credits.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.large is an entry-level general-purpose instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M processor at 3.1 GHz across 1 physical core, it maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes AVX-512 vector support, no bundled local storage, and a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest performance typical of small two-thread systems, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1212.0 and PassMark CPU score of 1995.98. While unsuited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, the dedicated vCPU allocation and predictable memory capacity make it practical for microservices, lightweight web servers, and development environments.
